Speaker, addressee, and sequence position are different deployments of the same action, not different things. Comparison frames include leaving the seat, ascending the seat, planting the staff, and returning to the abbot's quarters. Senses.Explanation: Gave a shout is the records' stock narrative formula for one performed vocal move in a public interview or teaching-seat event. Muzhou Daoming uses it after an unnamed monk shouts at him, asks what comes after three or four shouts, and strikes when no words follow. Feiyin Tongrong shouts amid a high-seat address and says that without stopping the entangling talk with a shout it would nearly have gone on without end (若不喝住，幾乎打葛藤無有了時也). Nanyue Falun Qitian performs four shouts in sequence and labels them respectively “the lion roars,” “the elephant king stretches,” “a mad dog chases a clod,” and “a shrimp cannot leap out of the dipper”; these are four stated comparisons, not four senses. Elsewhere an unnamed monk shouts and exits, Yunfu Zhi shouts before ascending the formal seat and offering incense, and Feiyin shouts before returning to the abbot's quarters. The same formula can close an address, combine with planting the staff, or precede questions to the assembly. Chan records preserve the shout as a positioned public move; the entry reports that position and any stated classification without assigning it an unstated force.
